The voice is warm, unhurried, and neutral in accent. 0–2 s: On a pale background, show an oval mitochondrial cutaway with a teal outer membrane, a darker folded inner membrane, and a cream matrix. At top center, display "Citric acid cycle" in large dark sans-serif lettering; retain this title throughout the film. 2–6 s: Gently enlarge the cutaway without cutting. brief: Make a 60-second widescreen explainer video on the citric acid cycle (the Krebs cycle) for first-year biology students. Show the cycle as a loop inside a mitochondrion: acetyl-CoA enters and joins oxaloacetate to form citrate, two carbons leave as CO2, NADH, FADH2 and ATP are produced along the way, and oxaloacetate is regenerated so the loop starts again. Label the key molecules on screen as they appear, under the title 'Citric acid cycle'. Calm English narration explaining each step as it happens. Simple clean 2D animation, no music.

research.subject: Citric acid cycle — research for one complete turn, shown inside a mitochondrion in 60 seconds. This is a biochemical episode, not a historical reenactment; no people, buildings or vessels are needed. Dates below are source publication dates, not dates when the reactions occurred.

looks.look: Documented structure: an oval-shaped organelle with an outer membrane and a folded inner membrane. The folds are cristae; the space enclosed by the inner membrane is the matrix. These are the structural features to retain in the simplified cutaway. ([openstax.org](https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/4-3-eukaryotic-cells))

Figure 29.14 documents an eight-step circular reaction diagram. The loop represents a sequence of reactions, not a physical circular structure inside the organelle. ([openstax.org](https://openstax.org/books/organic-chemistry/pages/29-7-the-citric-acid-cycle))

The source supplies chemical structure drawings: an acetyl group attached to coenzyme A through a thioester linkage, followed by citrate formation and release of CoA-SH. Use those drawings if molecular structures are required; do not invent literal molecular silhouettes. ([openstax.org](https://openstax.org/books/organic-chemistry/pages/29-7-the-citric-acid-cycle))

Documented structural formulas appear for oxaloacetate, citrate, isocitrate, α-ketoglutarate, succinyl-CoA, succinate, fumarate and malate. For the requested clean animation, their written names can replace detailed structures. The source does not establish a natural color for each molecule. ([openstax.org](https://openstax.org/books/organic-chemistry/pages/29-7-the-citric-acid-cycle))

Documented placement: embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane. Its FAD/FADH₂ carrier remains enzyme-bound; do not depict FADH₂ as a freely departing molecule. This source does not specify a detailed protein silhouette. ([openstax.org](https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/7-3-oxidation-of-pyruvate-and-the-citric-acid-cycle))

looks.thing: CO₂, NADH, FADH₂ and ATP output labels
looks.look: Figure 4.14 documents these outputs in a simplified cycle graphic. Use readable chemical labels rather than implying that colored badges are their actual microscopic appearance. Any palette is an explanatory design convention, not a sourced biological feature. ([openstax.org](https://openstax.org/books/concepts-biology/pages/4-3-citric-acid-cycle-and-oxidative-phosphorylation))

facts.fact: 0–6 seconds: Establish the mitochondrial matrix as the setting. In eukaryotic cells, this is where the citric acid cycle occurs. Title: 'Citric acid cycle'. ([openstax.org](https://openstax.org/books/concepts-biology/pages/4-3-citric-acid-cycle-and-oxidative-phosphorylation))

6–13 seconds: Acetyl-CoA supplies a two-carbon acetyl group, which combines with four-carbon oxaloacetate to form six-carbon citrate; coenzyme A is released. Show entry into the reaction loop, not acetyl-CoA crossing the inner membrane. ([openstax.org](https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/7-3-oxidation-of-pyruvate-and-the-citric-acid-cycle))
13–18 seconds: Citrate is rearranged into isocitrate. This is an isomerization, not a carbon-loss step. ([openstax.org](https://openstax.org/books/organic-chemistry/pages/29-7-the-citric-acid-cycle))

18–25 seconds: Isocitrate becomes five-carbon α-ketoglutarate, releasing the first CO₂ and producing the first NADH. ([openstax.org](https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/7-3-oxidation-of-pyruvate-and-the-citric-acid-cycle))

25–32 seconds: α-Ketoglutarate becomes four-carbon succinyl-CoA, releasing the second CO₂ and producing a second NADH. ([openstax.org](https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/7-3-oxidation-of-pyruvate-and-the-citric-acid-cycle))

32–38 seconds: Succinyl-CoA becomes succinate, producing ATP or GTP depending on the enzyme form. To match the brief, show ATP and add the small qualification 'GTP in some tissues'. ([openstax.org](https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/7-3-oxidation-of-pyruvate-and-the-citric-acid-cycle))

38–44 seconds: Succinate becomes fumarate as enzyme-bound FAD is reduced to FADH₂. Place this reaction beside the inner membrane. ([openstax.org](https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/7-3-oxidation-of-pyruvate-and-the-citric-acid-cycle))

44–52 seconds: Water is added to fumarate to form malate. Malate is then oxidized to regenerate oxaloacetate, producing the third NADH and closing the loop. ([openstax.org](https://openstax.org/books/organic-chemistry/pages/29-7-the-citric-acid-cycle))

52–60 seconds: Hold the regenerated loop and total the yield per acetyl-CoA: 2 CO₂, 3 NADH, 1 FADH₂ and 1 ATP equivalent. The reduced carriers supply electrons for subsequent ATP production. ([openstax.org](https://openstax.org/books/concepts-biology/pages/4-3-citric-acid-cycle-and-oxidative-phosphorylation))

Animation accuracy guardrail: the two carbons released as CO₂ on this turn are not the two acetyl carbons that have just entered. Do not color-track the incoming acetyl pair straight into the departing CO₂. ([openstax.org](https://openstax.org/books/concepts-biology/pages/4-3-citric-acid-cycle-and-oxidative-phosphorylation))

story.style: Widescreen, clean 2D animation with readable molecule labels, calm English narration explaining each reaction, and no music.
story.story:
0–6 seconds: Under “Citric acid cycle,” an oval mitochondrial cutaway reveals the outer membrane, folded inner membrane and matrix. Calm English narration introduces the reaction diagram.

6–13 seconds: Labeled acetyl-CoA enters the diagram, not across the membrane; its two-carbon acetyl group joins four-carbon oxaloacetate, forming six-carbon citrate and releasing coenzyme A.

13–18 seconds: Citrate rearranges into labeled isocitrate without carbon loss.

18–25 seconds: Isocitrate becomes five-carbon α-ketoglutarate; labels mark the first CO₂ and NADH.

25–32 seconds: α-Ketoglutarate becomes four-carbon succinyl-CoA, releasing the second CO₂ and producing a second NADH. Neither departing CO₂ is tracked from the incoming acetyl pair.

32–38 seconds: Succinyl-CoA becomes succinate; ATP appears with the small qualification “GTP in some tissues.”

38–44 seconds: Beside the inner membrane, succinate becomes fumarate; enzyme-bound FAD becomes FADH₂ and stays bound.

44–52 seconds: Water is added to fumarate, forming malate. Malate is oxidized, regenerating oxaloacetate and producing the third NADH to close the loop.

52–60 seconds: Hold the loop with totals per acetyl-CoA: 2 CO₂, 3 NADH, 1 FADH₂, 1 ATP equivalent. Narration explains that reduced carriers supply electrons for subsequent ATP production.
